text:
Predicates:
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x is a design style of y.
Adore(x, y) ::: x adores y.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
Style(x, y) ::: x is a style y.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
DesignBy(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.
HasDesignStyle(x, y) ::: x has style y.
Design(x) ::: x is a design.
Year(y) ::: y is a year.
Published(y, x) ::: y is published in year x.

Premises:
∀x (DesignStyle(x, z) ∧ Max(x) → InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: All of Max's design styles that he adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (Adore(x, y) ∧ Max(x) ∧ Brutalist(y) ∧ HasDesignStyle(z, y) → ¬InterestingGeometries(z)) ::: No brutalist building that Max adores has interesting geometries.
∀x (Adore(x, y) ∧ Max(x) → Style(y, z) ∨ Style(y, w)) ::: Every style that Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's style or Kelly Wearstler's style.
∀x (Style(x, KellyWearstler) ∧ Max(x) → Evocative(x)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler's styles that Max adores are evocative.
∀x (Style(x, KellyWearstler) ∧ Max(x) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All Kelly Wearstler's styles that Max adores are dreamy.
∀x (Design(x) ∧ Max(x) ∧ Adore(x, y) ∧ HasDesignStyle(z, y) ∧ InterestingGeometries(z) → Brutalist(z)) ::: If a Max design he adores has interesting geometries, then that design is a brutalist building. 

Conclusion:
DesignBy(max, z) → Brutalist(z)
